- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak if sentiment turns negative.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, especially after spikes; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.20.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, assume mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term trend reversal; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.  
- If forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average and sentiment is flat or negative, apply downward correction to prevent over-optimism.
